newsitem.title: USA: Bank, financial stocks soar with bond market.
newsitem.headline: Bank, financial stocks soar with bond market.

text.p: Interest-rate-sensitive bank and finacial stocks soared on Wednesday, spurred by a sharp drop in interest rates in the bond market.
With the yield on the 30-year Treasury bond at its lowest level since February 1996, the Philadelpha Stock Exchange's bank index jumped 16 points, or 2.4 percent, to 710.

Among active issues, Fannie Mae rose 2-7/16 to 45-15/16, Banc One Corp gained 3-3/16 to 56-1/2, Citicorp was up 3-15/16 to to 134-1/2, Chase Manhattan Corp gained 3-9/16 to 112-7/16 and J.P. Morgan & Co Inc rose 1-7/16 to 115-11/16.

"It appears that monetary policy will be benign in coming months, with interest rates more likely to fall or be unchanged than to rise," George Salem, banking industry analyst at Gerard Klauer Mattison, said in a report.
"Consequently, banks, the quintessential interest-sensitive equities, have a favorable environment for performance," he added. "We believe the group should be overweighted."
The long bond was up 26/32, its yield at 6.33 percent, its lowest level since the February 16, 1996 close.
The American Stock Exchange's broker-dealer index rose seven points, or one percent, to 724.

In late trading, Salomon Inc was up 1-4/16 to 59-15/16, A.G. Edwards Inc gained 1-3/16 to 41-1/8, Alex. Brown Inc rose 2-3/98 to 84-1/2, while Morgan Stanley Dean Witter Discover & Co gained 1-1/16 to 49-11/16.
Bucking the trend were Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette, off 1-9/16 to 67-1/8 and Merrill Lynch and Co Inc, off one to 68-1/8.
